Equilibrium and solution concepts
textPreview: Equilibrium and solution concepts

text: An equilibrium predicts stable behavior within stated assumptions. It does not guarantee safety in every real system.
textPreview: An equilibrium predicts stable behavior within stated assumptions. It does not guarantee safety in every real system.

text: Nash equilibrium
textPreview: Nash equilibrium

text: No player improves its utility by changing strategy alone while others remain fixed.
textPreview: No player improves its utility by changing strategy alone while others remain fixed.

text: Bayesian Nash equilibrium
textPreview: Bayesian Nash equilibrium

text: Each player acts under beliefs about hidden types, such as benign or malicious clients.
textPreview: Each player acts under beliefs about hidden types, such as benign or malicious clients.

text: Stackelberg equilibrium
textPreview: Stackelberg equilibrium

text: A leader commits to a strategy and a follower best-responds. The timing must be justified.

text: Definitions are standard game-theory terminology. The application to FL follows Sagduyu et al. (2023) for Nash reasoning and Li et al. (2024) for Bayesian Stackelberg reasoning.
